title: Campaign-backed scientific response experiments
summary: Freezes runtime evidence, composes serializable loading modes, lowers finite-difference perturbations to ordinary Campaign cases, and preserves first-passage localization and censoring.

science.statement: A derived response is evidence only when its baseline, perturbations, outputs, runtime identity, failures, and event-localization assumptions remain inspectable.

equations.label: central finite-difference response
equations.description: Each perturbed evaluation is a deterministic Campaign case rather than an anonymous solver call.

equations.label: linearly localized first passage
equations.description: The containing bracket and interpolation assumption remain part of the event record.

inputs.name: parameters and perturbations
inputs.type: bounded real ParameterSpace, baseline, and finite-difference steps
inputs.description: Defines the derivative coordinates and admissible perturbation cases.

inputs.name: response quantities
inputs.description: Fixes output order, shape, and units before any case is run.

outputs.name: ResponseReport
outputs.type: Jacobian, singular values, rank, condition number, nonlinearity and case identities
outputs.unit_role: output unit divided by parameter unit
outputs.description: A complete report only when every required perturbation succeeded.

outputs.name: FirstPassageEvent
outputs.unit_role: inherits history coordinate and response units
outputs.description: Retains the sample bracket and localization rule.

assumptions: Finite-difference parameters are continuous real quantities within declared bounds.
Linear first-passage localization assumes a continuous monitored response inside the sample bracket.
Every case is built fresh or safely reset by the Campaign builder.
conventions: Runtime compatibility is separate from scientific verification.
Central differences use baseline, plus, and minus cases with explicit absolute or relative steps.
A failed perturbation makes the response report incomplete.
applicability: Parameter sensitivity, actuator bases, inverse problems, local control studies, and response-space screening for deterministic FEM workflows.
limitations: Finite-difference cost grows with parameter dimension.
The first provider does not claim tangent-linear or adjoint differentiation.
Mixed-unit singular values and condition numbers require explicit nondimensional scaling.
Irreversible damage, contact, and topology changes can produce nonsmooth responses.

usage.minimal_example: operator = responses.finite_difference(parameter_space=space, baseline=baseline, outputs=quantities, perturbation=0.01); campaign_report, response = operator.run(build=build_case, evaluate=solve_case)

validation_rules: Reject non-finite or wrong-shaped response quantities.
Report missing perturbation cases instead of forming a partial Jacobian.
Preserve first-passage brackets and censoring state.
